national.canonicalTopic: National Green Tribunal environment and climate conference
national.headline: International conference on environment and climate dynamics inaugurated in New Delhi
facts: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the two-day conference “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics” in New Delhi on September 19, 2026.

The National Green Tribunal (NGT) organised the conference, with participation by environmental experts, judges from the Supreme Court, High Courts and District Courts, ministry secretaries and senior officials.

Participants included representatives of State Judicial Academies, State Legal Services Authorities, State Expert Appraisal Committees, State Environment Impact Assessment Authorities and State Wetland Authorities, as well as delegates from 17 countries.
Discussions addressed environmental and climate challenges, judicial approaches, scientific knowledge, governance, enforcement and institutional cooperation.
The NGT was established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010, on October 18, 2010; its principal bench is in New Delhi and its chairperson is Justice Prakash Shrivastava.
national.summary: The NGT-hosted conference brought legal, administrative and scientific participants together to discuss environmental and climate governance and implementation challenges.
national.staticLink: The National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 established a specialised tribunal for the effective and expeditious disposal of environmental cases.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The NGT was established on October 18, 2010, under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010; its principal bench is in New Delhi.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how judicial institutions and scientific expertise can improve environmental policy implementation and enforcement.

national.canonicalTopic: India’s flag bearers at Asian Games 2026
national.headline: Manu Bhaker and Pawan Sehrawat serve as India’s Asian Games flag bearers
facts: Shooter Manu Bhaker and shot-putter Tajinderpal Singh Toor were initially named as India’s opening-ceremony flag bearers; kabaddi player Pawan Sehrawat replaced Toor shortly before the ceremony.
The opening ceremony of the 20th Asian Games took place at Paloma Mizuho Stadium in Aichi–Nagoya, Japan, on 2026-09-19.
The Games ran from 2026-09-19 to 2026-10-04; the notes identify Honohon as the official mascot.
national.summary: Manu Bhaker and Pawan Sehrawat carried India’s flag at the opening ceremony after a last-minute change to the announced pair.
national.staticLink: The Asian Games are governed by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).
national.prelimsTakeaway: The 20th Asian Games were hosted by Aichi–Nagoya, Japan.
national.mainsAngle: Athlete representation and national identity in international multi-sport events.

sources.title: Manu Bhaker and Pawan Sehrawat Serve as India’s Flag Bearers at Asian Games–2026

# 2. Games details
| Basis | Details | Date / duration |
|---|---|---|
| Opening ceremony | **Paloma Mizuho Stadium**, **Aichi–Nagoya, Japan** | **September 19, 2026** |
| Games | **20th Asian Games** | **September 19 to October 4, 2026** |
| Official mascot | **Honohon** | — |

# 3. Governing body
- **Organisation:** **Olympic Council of Asia (OCA)** governs the Asian Games [GK]
- **⚠ Trap:** **Tajinderpal Singh Toor** was initially named as a flag bearer, but **Pawan Sehrawat** carried the flag after the late change
# 4. Also note
- The opening ceremony of the 20th Asian Games took place at Paloma Mizuho Stadium in Aichi–Nagoya, Japan, on 2026-09-19.
- The Games ran from 2026-09-19 to 2026-10-04; the notes identify Honohon as the official mascot.
> Exam angle: Identify India’s final opening-ceremony flag bearers at the **20th Asian Games** and distinguish the final pair from the initially announced pair.
